items.title: An operator is also included among participants
items.core_explanation_md:
A **system provider** operates an authorised payment system. A **system participant** can be a bank or another participating person and includes the provider. The provider and participant labels therefore are not mutually exclusive.

When investigating disruption, identify each role and its actual obligations. **Systemic risk** goes beyond an isolated inconvenience: one participant's inability to pay or a disruption may prevent others from meeting their obligations and threaten system stability. The definition focuses on the transmission and stability consequences, rather than the number of customer complaints alone.

self_check.prompt_text: Why can the same entity appear under both provider and participant labels?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The participant definition expressly includes the system provider.

items.title: Separate valuation, identification and recordkeeping functions
items.core_explanation_md:
A **derivative** derives its value from the specified underlying changes and is settled at a future date. A **legal entity identifier** identifies a person for the specified transactions; the **issuer** supplies that identifier. A **trade repository** handles electronic transaction records or data through functions such as collection, storage and dissemination.

These functions should not be conflated. Recording a derivative transaction is different from operating its settlement or bearing its payment obligation. Nor does an identifier itself authorise a provider to operate a payment system. Start with the activity actually carried out, then inspect the applicable legal requirements.

self_check.prompt_text: Does issuing an LEI by itself establish authorisation to operate a payment system?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Identification and payment-system operation are different functions with their own requirements.

items.title: Use the operative Board framework rather than mixing old and new names
items.core_explanation_md:
**RBI** is the designated authority under Section 3. The provision describes exercise of its powers through the **Payments Regulatory Board (PRB)**. Its statutory membership combines the RBI Governor as chairperson, the responsible Deputy Governor, one RBI officer nominated by the Central Board and three Central Government nominees. These are statutory roles, not a list of names to assume unchanged indefinitely.

The courseware retains an older BPSS description in one paragraph while later printing PRB provisions. The dated RBI FAQ and 2025 Gazette regulations support using the PRB framework. Keep the old name as historical context where needed; do not combine the former committee's composition with the new Board's provisions.

items.title: An application clock is not an operating licence
items.core_explanation_md:
Applying under Section 5 starts a process. Section 6 permits RBI to enquire into the particulars, operating capacity and other relevant matters. Section 7 addresses authorisation using considerations such as design, security, settlement, management, financial status and consumer interests.

The resulting authorisation states its effective date and conditions and can include fees and security. The six-month language is an **endeavour to dispose of the application**, not a rule that silence grants a licence. A project plan should therefore separate submission, enquiry responses, grant, effective date and compliance with conditions.

self_check.prompt_text: Does expiry of the six-month disposal endeavour itself establish permission to operate?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. It is not a deemed-authorisation rule.

items.title: Read the order and its route before advising on a challenge
items.core_explanation_md:
Refusal under Section 7 involves written reasons and a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Section 8 addresses revocation, including specified grounds and qualifications; the normal hearing provision is not the entire section because it has an additional exception. An order can also need safeguards for affected persons.

Section 9 gives the specified applicant or provider an appeal to the **Central Government**, covering refusal under Section 7(3) as well as revocation under Section 8. Its text uses communication of the order as the appeal-period trigger. Record the order and receipt evidence, then obtain the appropriate legal review; this batch does not grade an exact filing date.

self_check.prompt_text: Is the Section 9 route limited to revocation alone?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. It also covers the specified refusal of an authorisation application.

items.title: Build approval and notice into the change sequence
items.core_explanation_md:
A change affecting a payment system's structure or operation ordinarily needs **prior RBI approval**, followed by at least 30 days' notice to participants under Section 11. The provision also has a specific RBI power to permit the stated notice variation in monetary-policy or public-interest circumstances.

Do not reverse the sequence by counting advance days before approval as though they necessarily satisfy post-approval notice. Nor should internal sign-off or a response to RBI objections be treated as the final approval itself. A release checklist should identify the applicable change, approval and notice evidence.

self_check.prompt_text: Which event precedes the ordinary participant-notice period under Section 11?
self_check.expected_takeaway: RBI approval precedes the specified notice to system participants.

items.title: A scoped charge prohibition should not become an all-services rule
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 10A prohibits direct or indirect charges on persons making or receiving payments using the electronic modes prescribed under **Section 269SU** of the referenced tax legislation. Its scope depends on those prescribed modes.

A compliance review must identify the actual mode and the governing prescription. The courseware summary omits that scope qualification when broadly discussing charges; do not repeat it as a rule that every banking or payment service is free. Equally, relabelling a prohibited charge as indirect does not avoid the provision. Current mode prescriptions and any legislative cross-reference changes need verification before release.

self_check.prompt_text: What must be established before applying this particular charge prohibition?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Whether the payment uses a mode within the operative prescribed scope; indirect labels do not remove a covered charge.

items.title: Match the request to the power and the person who must respond
items.core_explanation_md:
A return request, access to information, entry to inspect equipment and an audit are related oversight tools with different statutory provisions. Sections 12–14 address information and inspection, including an officer authorised in writing for the entry/inspection power. Section 16 requires the provider and participants to assist RBI's audit or inspection.

A bank should record the authority, scope, documents requested, response owner and deadline. It should not assume that outsourcing the equipment to a vendor removes all participant responsibilities, or that a duty to provide information permits unrestricted disclosure to everyone.

self_check.prompt_text: Why should a bank distinguish access to information from entry and inspection?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The provisions identify different powers and conditions, including written authorisation for the specified inspecting officer.

items.title: Directions can require prevention and remedy, not just a report after loss
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 17 addresses specified conduct that creates or is likely to create inadequately controlled systemic risk or the stated wider effects. A written direction can require stopping the conduct or taking remedial action. Section 18 supports broader policy and written directions for payment-system regulation.

Under Section 19, the recipient complies without delay and reports compliance within the time allowed. The operational response therefore needs both the required action and the reporting evidence. A provider cannot treat the direction as optional merely because no loss has yet occurred, and filing a report does not replace actually carrying out the required remedy.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a compliance report alone satisfy a direction requiring a system change?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The action required by the direction and the reporting duty must both be addressed.

items.title: Protect information while making the disclosures the framework requires
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 15 concerns information RBI obtains under the specified provisions and contains qualified disclosure powers. Section 22 separately governs documents and information a provider receives from participants, with exceptions such as statutory requirements, consent and competent orders. Neither rule is accurately reduced to “disclose everything” or “never disclose anything”.

Providers also have duties under Sections 20–21 to operate within the Act, rules, authorisation and directions, and disclose relevant operating terms, charges, liability limits and netting documents to existing or potential participants. Make the required participant disclosure without assuming it grants a right to publish confidential participant records generally.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a duty to disclose operating terms to participants permit public disclosure of every participant record?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Operating-term disclosure and the qualified confidentiality duties concern different information and purposes.

items.title: Finality is a legal rule about an approved determination
items.core_explanation_md:
Gross settlement processes separate instructions. Netting offsets obligations according to the approved arrangement to determine net positions. Neither label lets a participant select its own method contrary to the system's approved procedure.

Section 23 supports the prescribed finality and loss-allocation framework. Its explanation makes the determination final and irrevocable under the section whether or not the resulting money or other assets have actually been paid. That does not mean the unpaid obligation disappears. It means finality and cash completion are different facts.

A **central counterparty** interposes through novation. The section includes specific protections when insolvency affects a participant or the CCP, and requires return of excess collateral after permitted appropriation. Do not replace those conditions with a universal statement that insolvency cancels final settlements or allows all collateral to be retained.

self_check.prompt_text: Can a final net determination coexist with money still to be paid?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Yes. The statutory finality explanation distinguishes determination from actual payment; the payment obligation still needs to be met.

items.title: Reconcile a net position before discussing its funding
items.core_explanation_md:
In an illustrative approved netting arrangement, participant Alder owes Birch **Rs 1,80,000** and Cedar **Rs 70,000**. Birch owes Alder **Rs 90,000**, and Cedar owes Alder **Rs 40,000**. Alder's outgoing total is **Rs 2,50,000** and incoming total is **Rs 1,30,000**, leaving a **Rs 1,20,000 net debit**.

This arithmetic identifies the net payment obligation under the stated arrangement. It does not prove that every system uses multilateral netting, that the money has already been paid, or that collateral and loss-allocation rules can be ignored. Those questions require the authorised system's approved procedures.

self_check.prompt_text: Does the computed net debit prove that the settlement cash has already moved?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The position calculation and the actual payment are separate facts.

items.final_answer_with_unit: 120000 rupees net debit for Alder under the stated netting arrangement.

items.title: The Act, regulations and an operator's permission do different jobs
items.core_explanation_md:
**Section 38** authorises RBI to make regulations consistent with the Act. The listed matters include governance procedure, application/authorisation forms, payment-instruction standards and information returns. A regulation develops the statutory framework; it is not the same document as an individual operator's authorisation.

For a compliance file, retain the relevant Act provision, the regulation version and the operator's actual permission and conditions. Reading only an old summary of an application form cannot establish that a new service is authorised or that all current reporting requirements have been met.

items.title: Use the regulation's own version and commencement evidence
items.core_explanation_md:
The dated RBI FAQ distinguishes the **Payment and Settlement Systems Regulations, 2008** from the **Payments Regulatory Board Regulations, 2025**. Their subjects differ: system application/authorisation, standards and returns on one side, and Board governance on the other. A courseware note ending at a 2022 amendment does not show that the regulation set stops there.

Section 38 includes effective-date and parliamentary-laying provisions. Use the operative text and notification evidence for the relevant exam cutoff; do not infer commencement from a website folder, a PDF creation timestamp or a document identifier. Sanctions also need their own provisions and review rather than a generic penalty number copied into every situation.

items.title: Build a security file around the obligation and the property
items.core_explanation_md:
For a mortgage analysis, identify **whose interest is being offered, which specific immovable property it concerns, and what obligation it secures**. Section 58(a) is not limited to a loan already disbursed. It also addresses money to be advanced, existing or future debt and an engagement that may create a monetary liability.

The person transferring the interest is the **mortgagor**; the recipient is the **mortgagee**. The secured principal and interest are the mortgage-money. The instrument, if any, effecting the transfer is the mortgage-deed. These roles should be traced to the documents rather than assumed from who visits the branch.

An outright sale for an independent purchase price and a transfer structured to secure a debt have different purposes. Inspect the operative arrangement; a document label or the word security alone does not finish the classification.

self_check.prompt_text: Must the advance already have been disbursed for section 58(a) to be relevant?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The definition includes money to be advanced and the stated future-debt or monetary-liability purposes.

items.title: Separate the lending shorthand from the statutory category
items.core_explanation_md:
Banking files often use **charge** broadly for a security interest. Section 100 uses a more particular immovable-property category: property is made security for payment, but the transaction does **not amount to a mortgage**. That statutory distinction should be preserved when a question asks which legal arrangement was created.

Do not infer a mortgage merely because a sanction letter calls something collateral. Equally, do not treat every reference to a charge as proof that no mortgage exists. The underlying transaction, property and transfer of interest must be examined. A valid secured transaction also needs the applicable formalities and authority; classification is not a substitute for those checks.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is the word charge in a sanction letter insufficient to settle the statutory classification?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The underlying transaction may be a mortgage or another security arrangement; section 100 has a specific scope.

items.title: Compare simple and English mortgages using the operative promises
items.core_explanation_md:
A **simple mortgage** combines a personal repayment undertaking with a right to cause sale of the property on default, without delivery of possession. The mortgagee is not made the person entitled to take the property's income merely by that classification.

An **English mortgage** combines personal repayment on a specified date with transfer of the property subject to retransfer on the agreed repayment. Its name does not mean that the document is governed by English law or concerns property in England. Inspect both the repayment covenant and retransfer terms. The classification itself does not establish an unrestricted power to sell without court; remedies have separate statutory conditions.

self_check.prompt_text: Does the label English mortgage alone establish an unconditional out-of-court sale power?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Classification and the conditions of the applicable remedy must be checked separately.

items.title: Distinguish a conditional sale structure from an income-based security
items.core_explanation_md:
A **mortgage by conditional sale** uses an ostensible sale subject to the specified repayment/default condition. Section 58(c) requires that condition to appear in the document that effects or purports to effect the sale. A separate promise does not automatically satisfy that same-document requirement.

A **usufructuary mortgage** instead centres on possession, or the undertaking to deliver it, and authority to receive rents and profits toward interest, principal or the stated combination. The accounting for those receipts matters to the secured obligation and recovery of possession. Avoid adding an automatic ownership rule based solely on the number of years in possession. Different covenants and hybrid arrangements require their own analysis.

self_check.prompt_text: What document-location qualification matters for the conditional-sale classification?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The relevant condition must be embodied in the document effecting or purporting to effect the sale.

items.title: Use the residual type only after reading the full arrangement
items.core_explanation_md:

items.title: Do not confuse custody for inspection with creation of security
items.core_explanation_md:
A bank may hold property documents for valuation, legal examination, safe custody or security creation. These are different purposes. Section 58(f) requires title-document delivery to the creditor or agent **with intention to create security**. The file should therefore explain why the documents were delivered and how that intention is evidenced.

A receipt saying documents were taken for scrutiny should not be silently rewritten as a concluded mortgage. Conversely, the absence of a conventional mortgage-deed label does not answer whether a valid title-deed deposit occurred. Assess debt, documents, delivery, intention and the relevant legal conditions together.

items.title: Read the formality rule together with its limits
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 59 sets a central-text rule for mortgages securing principal of Rs 100 or more, other than a mortgage by deposit of title deeds: the specified registered instrument, mortgagor signature and at least two attesting witnesses are required. Its smaller-amount rules also have qualifications.

The function of a memorandum, applicable state amendments, stamp law and separate filing obligations need their own sources. Classification under section 58(f) and the formalities of a particular instrument are connected questions, but they are not interchangeable.

items.title: Do not decide competing rights from the registry timestamps alone
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 48 of the Transfer of Property Act gives a general earlier-created-right rule where competing rights cannot all operate fully together, subject to the stated special-contract or reservation qualification. Section 47 of the Registration Act concerns when a registered document operates: it does not simply choose the day registration occurred.

For a hypothetical pair of valid instruments stipulated to operate from execution, a later registration timestamp alone does not prove later priority. Record creation, operative effect, registration, validity and any binding priority arrangement. The title-deed-mortgage proviso in Registration Act section 48 is another reason not to apply an unqualified “registered always defeats unregistered” shortcut.

items.core_explanation_md:
In a usufructuary arrangement, the mortgagee may retain the specified possession and appropriate rents or profits as the arrangement permits. A bank examining the property must therefore distinguish **possession held as security** from a later claimed ownership right. The receipts and their agreed application to interest or principal matter.

Section 62 addresses the mortgagor's recovery of possession when its conditions are met. An underwriting file should obtain the mortgage terms, account of receipts, payments or deposits and the legal basis for any asserted change in title. Length of possession alone is not that complete evidence.

self_check.expected_takeaway: Possession may continue as part of the security arrangement; discharge, accrual and any valid title-changing event need examination.

items.title: Read the deciding holding, not an isolated time-period summary
items.core_explanation_md:

items.title: Ask what the document proves about the offered interest
items.core_explanation_md:
A property file can contain a conveyance, a chain document, a revenue receipt, a valuation and a search result. They perform different evidentiary jobs. The question for mortgage scrutiny is what right the offered documents establish and whether the person creating security can offer that interest. A record that supports payment of a tax is not automatically conclusive proof of the full title offered as collateral.

Section 58(f) uses **documents of title**. The bank should examine the documents and chain rather than relabel every property-related paper a title deed. The courseware cites judicial discussions on sufficiency; those decisions still require independent checking for release. This lesson does not declare a live property title valid.

items.title: A copy requires a reasoned exception enquiry, not an automatic answer
items.core_explanation_md:
If the file contains a copy, record whether it is certified, why the original is unavailable, who may hold the original, the chain and search evidence, and the applicable legal requirements. These are enquiry points, not a promise that a particular checklist makes the copy legally sufficient.

The courseware's categorical statements about copies and its description of registry safeguards are not independently verified here. self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The legal sufficiency, circumstances and applicable requirements still need a reasoned determination.

items.title: Foreclosure, sale and a personal money claim are different remedies
items.core_explanation_md:
**Foreclosure** concerns barring the right to redeem; a **sale** seeks sale of the property toward the secured amount. A credit file should identify the mortgage form, the obligations and the provision relied on before presenting a recovery route. A personal repayment covenant and a property remedy also need to be distinguished. Do not infer every remedy from a generic security label or from the fact that a default occurred.

items.title: Read the payment instruction before choosing a debt
items.core_explanation_md:
When one debtor owes several distinct debts to a creditor, allocation is a separate decision from receiving the money. Start with **express or implied indication by the debtor**. If the bank accepts a payment accompanied by a valid direction to a particular debt, section 59 requires application accordingly. The bank should preserve the instruction and explain how its posting implements it.

Only when the debtor has omitted an indication and the circumstances do not indicate a debt does section 60 give the creditor the stated discretion among lawful debts actually due and payable. An internal preference for a secured exposure cannot erase an accepted debtor instruction. A debt need not be legally recoverable by suit to be eligible under section 60, but this does not mean the payment automatically revives every time-barred remedy.

self_check.prompt_text: May a bank silently redirect an accepted payment away from the debt expressly designated by its debtor?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The accepted payment must follow the express or implied indication under section 59.

items.title: The default rule follows time, then proportion
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 61 addresses the remaining situation: **neither party appropriates**. Apply the payment to debts in order of time. If relevant debts have equal standing, divide proportionately rather than giving every debt the same rupee amount. Record which rule the file actually invokes; chronological default is not the first step while a debtor direction remains operative.

For a proportional split, multiply the available payment by each debt divided by the equal-standing total. Check that allocations add back to the payment and do not exceed the debt being discharged. The examples here assume the stated debts alone, no competing appropriation and exact whole-rupee results. Interest, later payments and disputed debt status would need their own inputs.

self_check.prompt_text: Why does an equal-standing allocation need the debt amounts, not merely the number of debts?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The statutory fallback is proportional to the debts, so unequal debts do not receive equal rupee allocations.

items.title: Assignment changes the recipient of a right
items.core_explanation_md:
An assignment transfers a right or benefit from the **assignor** to the **assignee**. It should not be treated as a unilateral means of imposing a new contractual burden on someone else. For an actionable claim within section 130, identify the signed written transfer and its scope. The statute makes the described transfer complete on execution; notice serves a different protective function.

The assignee may pursue the transferred claim in its own name under the provision. That does not turn every commercial right into the same statutory category: Chapter VIII has exclusions, and insurance has specific rules. Classify the asset and governing regime before applying a generic assignment checklist.

self_check.prompt_text: Does describing an arrangement as assignment prove that every contractual obligation has moved without any other party assent?

items.title: A complete transfer still needs attention to notice
items.core_explanation_md:
Execution and debtor notification must be tracked separately. Section 130 does not postpone every transfer until the debtor receives notice, yet its proviso protects the specified dealings where the debtor is neither a party to the transfer nor has received the required express notice. A completed assignment with an unaddressed notice gap can therefore carry a collection risk.

Section 131 calls for written notice, the required signature and the assignee name and address; it specifies the alternative signature route if the transferor refuses to sign. Preserve the actual notice and receipt evidence. A bank should not assume that a private assignment file automatically informed the debtor.

self_check.expected_takeaway: The debtor-dealing proviso protects specified dealings before the stated participation/notice condition is met.

items.title: Buying a claim does not automatically cleanse its defects
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 132 makes the assignee take subject to the liabilities and equities affecting the transferor in respect of the claim at the transfer date. Due diligence should therefore ask about disputes, defences and existing adjustments, rather than look only at the face amount and assignment price. The assignee lack of knowledge does not by itself supply better rights under this rule.

Keep the statutory scope in view: the chapter does not apply to specified negotiable instruments and mercantile documents of title, and it restricts dealings by certain persons connected with courts. The courseware discusses particular judicial exceptions; those have not been converted into general rules in this draft.

self_check.prompt_text: Can the assignee rely only on having paid value and being unaware of a pre-existing equity?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Section 132 preserves the applicable liabilities and equities as at transfer.

items.title: A pledge needs more than a security label
items.core_explanation_md:
A pledge is a bailment of goods serving a security purpose. Identify the goods, the secured obligation and the delivery or legally effective control arrangement. Actual relocation is not the only possible form of delivery, but a document that merely says goods are pledged does not prove the bank has the required possession or control.

An original enquiry is to ask who can release the goods, whose instructions the custodian follows and what evidence changes that position. A warehouse acknowledgement may matter to constructive delivery; its effect requires the facts and applicable law. Do not infer effective control solely from an inventory list, a signboard or the bank having visited the warehouse.

self_check.prompt_text: Why does the file need to identify who can order release of the goods?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The pledge enquiry includes delivery and effective control, not merely a label or physical stock list.

items.title: Check authority without assuming every possessor is an owner
items.core_explanation_md:
The owner is not the only possible valid pledgor, but exceptions are conditional. Under section 178, examine how a mercantile agent obtained possession, the ordinary course of the agent business, good faith and notice of lack of authority. Those conditions cannot be replaced by possession alone. Section 178A separately concerns the specified unrescinded voidable-contract situation.

Section 179 limits a pledge made by someone who has only a limited interest to that interest. The credit decision should therefore distinguish ownership, authority and the value of the interest actually offered. None of these provisions turns every unauthorised pledge into good security merely because the lender acted politely or took a signed declaration.

self_check.prompt_text: Does possession by a mercantile agent alone settle the section 178 enquiry?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Owner consent to possession, ordinary course, good faith and the notice qualification also matter.

items.title: Identify why each retained amount is secured
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 173 covers retention for the secured obligation, interest and necessary expenses of possession or preservation. A review should match each claimed amount to its legal or contractual basis. An unrelated debt should not be silently added just because the bank already holds the goods.

Section 174 supplies the other-debt qualification and a distinct presumption concerning subsequent advances, subject to anything contrary. Record relevant contract terms and the timing of advances. The useful question is not whether the customer owes anything at all, but whether this retention covers the particular amount under the applicable rule.

self_check.expected_takeaway: Section 174 requires the relevant contract basis, subject to its qualified subsequent-advance presumption.

items.title: Expense recovery and permission to retain are different
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 175 entitles the pawnee to receive extraordinary expenses incurred for preservation. Distinguish that recovery entitlement from section 173 retention for necessary possession or preservation expenses. Do not assume every extraordinary invoice automatically supplies the same statutory retention power without reviewing the governing terms and rule.

The bank also owes care as bailee. Under section 151, compare its conduct with what an ordinarily prudent person would do for goods of the same bulk, quality and value in similar circumstances. Section 152 qualifies responsibility where the required care is taken and no special contract applies. Insurance and a warehouse receipt do not replace a reasoned custody and care plan.

self_check.prompt_text: Does the existence of insurance itself establish that the bank exercised the required bailment care?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The statutory care standard concerns the bank conduct in the circumstances.

items.title: Default creates options with conditions
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 176 distinguishes suing on the obligation while retaining collateral from selling the pledged goods after reasonable notice. A lender should identify the route and satisfy its conditions. Default is not itself a transfer of full ownership, an instruction to sell immediately or permission to keep an excess realisation.

If sale proceeds fall short, the stated debt balance remains payable; if they exceed the amount due, account for the surplus to the pawnor. The arithmetic must use the amounts legally included in the file. A calculation question can assume those components are established, but that assumption cannot certify which real charges are enforceable.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a pledge label alone eliminate the reasonable-notice condition for a sale?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Section 176 conditions the sale route on reasonable notice.

items.title: Redemption is tied to actual sale, not merely overdue status
items.core_explanation_md:
Under section 177, a defaulting pawnor can redeem before the actual sale by meeting the stated obligation and default-related expenses. The scheduled repayment date having passed does not alone extinguish that right. Record the relevant sale stage and redemption request rather than treating overdue status as automatic forfeiture.

The courseware also describes case-law qualifications where a pawnee seeks recovery but cannot return the goods. Those judgments require separate verification and are not reduced here to a universal litigation result. This draft does not set a fixed reasonable-notice period, approve a particular sale or decide disputed enforcement facts.

self_check.prompt_text: Is expiry of the original repayment date alone the end of section 177 redemption?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The provision permits the stated redemption before actual sale, including default-related expenses.

items.title: Borrower possession changes the control problem
items.core_explanation_md:
Hypothecation charges movable property while possession remains undelivered to the secured creditor. The borrower may need the goods for production or daily trade, so ongoing stock integrity becomes a central credit-control issue. Do not rewrite a charge as the bank becoming the absolute owner of every item, or describe a borrower-held arrangement as a proved pledge without examining delivery.

The statutory definition includes existing and future movables and the stated floating-charge features. Those words describe the security form; they do not establish every condition for enforcement. SARFAESI also has express exclusions, including the specified lien and movable-pledge categories. The remedy needs its own applicability analysis.

self_check.prompt_text: What central possession distinction separates the described hypothecation from a pledge enquiry?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The hypothecation definition involves no delivery of possession to the secured creditor; pledge depends on bailment for security.

items.title: Treat stock reporting as a claim to verify
items.core_explanation_md:
Where goods stay with the borrower, a monthly stock statement is information rather than proof that all listed goods exist, remain valuable and are free of other claims. Compare statements with inspections, records, permitted stock movements, title and charge searches, insurance and the agreed controls. A signboard is a notice aid, not a substitute for these enquiries.

The courseware highlights obsolete stock, substitution, disposal and multiple financing as risks. Build the review around the identified risk: for example, investigate stock-age deterioration even if total reported value is unchanged. Covenants on disclosure, further charges, insurance and inspection should be read with the actual agreement and applicable law. No generic clause by itself establishes current priority or permits immediate possession-taking.

self_check.prompt_text: Why can an unchanged total stock value still need investigation?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The quantity, quality, age, title and composition may have changed even when the reported total is unchanged.

items.title: A signed charge and a registered charge are different file stages
items.core_explanation_md:
For a company security, keep creation evidence, the applicable filing duty, actual registration and the certificate distinct. Section 77 addresses registration with the Registrar and a certificate following registration. A signed hypothecation agreement alone is not evidence that the statutory registration step is complete.

The inspected section also separates treatment of the charge by the liquidator or another creditor from the underlying repayment obligation. Section 77(3) sets its registration/certificate condition; section 77(4) preserves the repayment contract or obligation. Do not translate a filing failure into an assertion that the borrower automatically owes nothing. Other registries and applicable law may impose additional requirements.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Section 77(4) preserves the repayment contract/obligation despite the section 77(3) qualification.

items.core_explanation_md:
Section 171 concerns a general balance of account and goods bailed to a banker, subject to contrary contract. The courseware further explains lawful possession in ordinary banking business and a purpose inconsistent with general lien. Examine how and why the bank obtained the property before treating every item held on its premises as general security.

Documents left for a specific safe-custody purpose raise a different enquiry from goods received as security in ordinary business. A general customer debt does not settle that difference. Do not infer an unrestricted power of sale or a right over every deposit simply from the wording of the statutory retainer provision; those require their own legal basis and conditions.

self_check.prompt_text: Why must the bank preserve the purpose for which property was delivered?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A specific purpose or contrary contract can be inconsistent with the general retainer claim.

items.title: Set-off concerns mutual obligations, not just shared names
items.core_explanation_md:
Set-off concerns adjusting reciprocal monetary claims. The courseware requires attention to the same parties in the same legal capacity and to debts that are sufficiently certain and due. An account holder acting as trustee is not necessarily holding money in the same capacity as a personal borrower. A shared name in two records does not settle mutuality.

Separate present debt from a future or contingent exposure. A guarantee not yet crystallised or a debt not yet due raises conditions that cannot be ignored merely because the bank also holds a credit balance. Actual account terms, trust notice, joint ownership, applicable law and any required demand or notice must be checked. This draft does not authorise a transfer from a live account.

self_check.prompt_text: Does matching a person name alone establish the same-capacity requirement?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The legal capacity and reciprocal obligations need separate examination.

items.title: Give each proposed adjustment its own reason
items.core_explanation_md:
Lien and set-off are not interchangeable labels. A file seeking to retain goods should identify the property, bailment purpose and retainer basis. A file seeking to combine account balances should identify the reciprocal debts, capacity, maturity and authority for the adjustment. Presenting either as a general right to take any customer asset hides the deciding facts.

The courseware includes special partnership combinations and events said to trigger automatic set-off. Those conclusions need primary authority and insolvency, garnishee and notice analysis before publication. Use the general distinction to ask better questions; do not convert this draft into a universal partnership, joint-account or insolvency rule.

self_check.prompt_text: What should an adjustment note record besides the amounts?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The legal route, parties/capacities, maturity, purpose restrictions and relevant contractual or statutory conditions.

items.title: Start with the secured interest, not the lending product name
items.core_explanation_md:
For company-law purposes, a charge is the described interest or lien created as security on company property, assets or undertakings; the definition includes a mortgage. A facility name does not determine whether its security creates such an interest. Identify the chargor, the property or undertaking and the obligation secured.

Section 77 has broad language concerning property, location and tangible or other assets, with statutory qualifications including prescribed exemptions. Do not use the former 1956 Act list as an exhaustive current checklist or turn a courseware exception into a universal filing exemption. A guarantee and a proprietary security interest also require separate classification; the label alone should not decide the filing result.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is the lending product name insufficient to determine whether a company charge exists?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The enquiry concerns the security interest actually created on the company property, assets or undertaking.

items.title: A floating charge needs its terms and the actual event
items.core_explanation_md:
The courseware contrasts security attached to identified property with a floating arrangement covering a changing class of assets while ordinary business dealings continue within the arrangement. Crystallisation describes the charge attaching on the relevant event. It does not mean every floating charge already controls every individual asset in the same way as fixed security.

Read the instrument for the asset class, permitted dealings, event and effect; then check applicable law. A receiver appointment, business cessation or contractual event may be relevant, but a phrase in a stock report cannot replace proof of the event. Nor does crystallisation by itself establish an absolute priority over every competing statutory or insolvency claim.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a floating-charge label prove that a crystallisation event has already occurred?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The relevant terms, event and legal consequences must be established.

items.title: Creation, submission and registration are different events
items.core_explanation_md:
Keep the signed instrument, creation facts, application, actual registration and certificate as distinct evidence. The file must identify the company, chargeholder, secured assets and scope of the charge, with the prescribed particulars and instrument where applicable. Submitting a form does not by itself prove that the Registrar registered the charge or issued its certificate.

For the duty under section 77, the text starts with thirty days from creation. Late-registration routes are conditional and version-specific. A bank should diarise the applicable filing obligation and retain the actual result rather than assume an application receipt completes every security requirement. This draft is not a filing calendar for a live transaction.

self_check.prompt_text: What evidence is still needed after an application receipt?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The actual registration result and certificate, with the applicable legal and filing requirements.

items.title: Do not add every extension to every new charge
items.core_explanation_md:
The inspected section 77 provisos distinguish charges by their creation regime. Its later-charge route describes a period measured from creation and a further conditional period, with application and prescribed fees. It does not give an automatic extension or make the older three-hundred-day route available to every new charge.

The courseware own tables distinguish historical regimes, while its earlier unit contains a broader summary. Use the controlling provision and rules applicable at the exam cutoff, not whichever summary offers more time. The retained Act is consolidated after cutoff, so exact form versions, fees, transitional conditions and calendar treatment require independent verification before release.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a conditional late-registration route amount to automatic acceptance of a late filing?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The applicable regime, application, fee and other conditions still matter.

items.title: The chargeholder has a separate statutory application route
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 78 addresses the specified company failure to register and permits an application by the person in whose favour the charge was created. The Registrar process includes the company opportunity stated in the provision. The chargeholder route is therefore different from pretending that the company filed on time.

Where registration is effected on that application, the section permits the stated fees or additional fees to be recovered from the company. Record who applied, under which provision, the notices and actual outcome. Do not infer either that only the company can ever initiate registration or that the chargeholder can bypass every condition.

self_check.prompt_text: Why should the file record who made the registration application?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The chargeholder statutory route has its own trigger, process and fee-recovery consequences.

items.title: Deemed notice and priority answer different questions
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 80 links deemed notice to registration for a person acquiring the described property, assets, undertaking or interest. Notice is not itself a complete priority decision between every possible claimant. Section 77 also says subsequent registration must not prejudice rights acquired before the charge is actually registered.

A ranking opinion needs the interests, relevant dates, instrument terms, applicable statutory regime and any agreed ranking. Do not reduce it to the first registration timestamp in all circumstances. In particular, late registration should not be represented as silently erasing an intervening right simply because a certificate eventually exists.

self_check.prompt_text: Does deemed notice under section 80 by itself rank every competing claim?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. It addresses notice; priority requires the applicable rights and governing rules.

items.title: A filing failure does not make the loan balance disappear
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 77(3) restricts the described treatment of a company-created charge by a liquidator or another creditor unless the stated registration and certificate requirements are met. Section 77(4) then expressly preserves the repayment contract or obligation. Keep those consequences separate in a security report.

The difference matters because a lender may have an outstanding monetary claim while failing to establish the security position it expected. Conversely, a registration certificate does not prove that every underlying title, priority or enforcement question is settled. This lesson asks for an accurate description of evidence and legal consequence, not a real insolvency distribution outcome.

self_check.prompt_text: What remains distinct from recognition of the registered charge?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The contract or obligation to repay the secured money.

items.core_explanation_md:
A security can change after creation. Section 83 allows the Registrar to act on the specified evidence even where no company intimation has been received. The power is conditional on the Registrar being satisfied about the statutory facts; it is not an automatic update whenever a bank sends an email. The provision also requires the affected parties to be informed after the entry.

Section 82 has its own notice process and a qualification where the specified form is signed by the holder. Do not carry forward a summary that every satisfaction case always follows an identical notice path. The courseware satisfaction-form label is held back pending primary rules/form evidence; filing and the Registrar certification are different actions.

self_check.prompt_text: What must support an entry under section 83 when company intimation is absent?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Evidence satisfying the Registrar of the specified satisfaction or release facts and compliance with the applicable process.

items.title: The event and the person responsible must be identified
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 84 concerns the described receiver or manager appointment. It addresses both an appointment order and appointment under a power in an instrument, with the relevant notice and supporting copy to the company and Registrar. Identify the actual route, date and responsible person rather than assume only a court-order case can engage the section.

The provision has a stated notice period, but applying it to a real calendar requires the governing facts and rules. Appointment is a management or recovery event; it does not itself prove that the secured debt is paid or that the charge should be recorded as satisfied. Keep the event record and security discharge evidence separate.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Appointment and debt satisfaction are separate events.

items.title: Cessation is another record event
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 84 also requires the appointed person to notify the company and Registrar on ceasing to hold the appointment, with registration of that notice. A file that records only the original appointment may therefore remain incomplete after the role ends. Track the cessation fact rather than silently deleting the appointment record.

This recordkeeping distinction should not be turned into an enforcement power. Whether the receiver was validly appointed, what powers the instrument gives and what insolvency or other regime applies require their own legal review. The lesson concerns identifying the statutory event and keeping its evidence, not approving a live recovery action.

items.title: A deliberate false statement is not just another late fee
items.core_explanation_md:
The inspected section 86 distinguishes default in compliance with the charge chapter from wilfully furnishing false or incorrect information or knowingly suppressing material information required under section 77. The latter provision points to section 447 action. A processing checklist should therefore distinguish missing a filing step from deliberate misinformation.

Do not teach that payment of an ordinary late fee automatically cleanses a false declaration. Equally, do not infer a proven wilful offence from any data mismatch without examining the facts and statutory elements. This draft does not decide liability or impose a penalty; its source and cutoff applicability remain subject to independent review.

self_check.prompt_text: Why should an incorrect record not automatically be labelled deliberate fraud?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The statutory wording includes wilfulness or knowledge qualifications that need factual examination.

items.title: Rectification must fit the statutory problem
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 87 addresses specified omissions in satisfaction intimation and omissions or misstatements in filings previously made concerning the described charge records. Its grounds and terms must be considered. Correcting a misstatement in an existing filing and extending time for omitted satisfaction intimation are not identical to registering every never-filed new charge.

The courseware broad extension summary should therefore not become an unrestricted rescue rule. Identify what was filed, what was omitted or misstated, the affected parties and the relief the statute actually permits. Evidence of an accidental error does not by itself establish that every requested remedy is within scope. Current rules and the competent process also need verification.

self_check.prompt_text: Why must a rectification request identify the earlier filing and the precise defect?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The statutory scope depends on the kind of omission/misstatement or satisfaction-intimation issue, rather than a universal power to cure any charge problem.

items.title: Choose the scheme version before applying its procedure
items.core_explanation_md:
This unit examines the **2021 scheme as at 30 June 2026**, read with the identified amendments and coverage notification. It is not a current instruction to file a complaint under an obsolete scheme. items.title: A receipt channel is not an eligibility decision
items.core_explanation_md:
The 2021 scheme provides online registration through the designated portal and electronic or physical submission to CRPC; complaints received directly at RBI offices are to be forwarded for further action. RBI appoints the Ombudsman and Deputy Ombudsman from its officers, for a term not exceeding three years at a time. The scheme distinguishes their powers, including the Deputy role in specified closures and facilitated settlements. The statutory role should not be inferred from a job title used in an internal bank escalation.

items.title: Representation and the amount in dispute need separate checks
items.core_explanation_md:
A complaint can be made personally or through a duly authorised representative under the scheme conditions. The advocate restriction has the stated exception when the advocate is the aggrieved person; it should not be turned into a rule that an advocate can never bring their own complaint.

Clause 8 also distinguishes the amount in dispute from the Ombudsman compensation powers. The compensation ceiling is not a universal ceiling on the disputed transaction amount. items.title: Confidentiality does not prevent the stated fair-process disclosures
items.core_explanation_md:

items.title: A response deadline and a granted extension are different
items.core_explanation_md:
The 2021 framework calls for the regulated entity written version and relied-on documents within the stated period. Further time may be granted on the written request described in clause 14(3). This does not mean the complainant automatically proves every claim by silence; it means the entity cannot assume that ignoring the process is a neutral strategy.

items.title: A settlement needs the parties actual agreement
items.core_explanation_md:

items.title: Public information and a nodal role support the complaint process
items.core_explanation_md:
The 2021 scheme requires a Principal Nodal Officer at the stated seniority, responsible for representation and furnishing information. The entity also has branch and website information duties: prominent contact/portal details, salient features in the stated languages and a scheme copy available for customer reference. Naming an officer internally does not by itself perform those public-information duties.

RBI suspension under clause 2 is a different matter. It requires an RBI order and may concern all or specified clauses, generally or for a specified entity, with the stated extension power. An entity cannot create its own scheme suspension merely because its nodal officer is absent or its complaint queue is busy.

self_check.prompt_text: Can an RE suspend the scheme itself simply because the appointed nodal officer is unavailable?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Clause 2 addresses RBI ordered suspension, while the entity information and staffing arrangements need their own compliance.

items.title: A label does not establish every statutory benefit
items.core_explanation_md:
Start a supplier file with two separate questions: what is the enterprise category, and does the party meet the definition needed for the particular protection? The Act recognises manufacturing and service enterprises. Its delayed-payment chapter concerns eligible micro and small suppliers; a medium classification does not by itself establish that eligibility.

Section 2(n) also includes specified bodies such as NSIC and State Small Industries Development Corporations, and the described bodies selling MSE goods or rendering their services. Check the actual statutory route rather than assuming every business using an MSME logo qualifies. Registration timing and later case law need their own review.

self_check.prompt_text: Can a medium classification alone establish delayed-payment supplier status?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Classification and the relevant supplier definition are distinct checks.

items.title: Test both dimensions against the dated ceiling
items.core_explanation_md:
For the 2025 classification framework effective from 1 April 2025, micro requires investment no more than INR 2.5 crore and turnover no more than INR 10 crore. The corresponding small limits are INR 25 crore and INR 100 crore; medium limits are INR 125 crore and INR 500 crore. A category needs both tests, so one low figure cannot cancel the other figure exceeding its ceiling.

These replace the older classification values printed in the book. Use the classification date stated in the question. The principal notification also provides common-PAN aggregation and exclusion of export turnover for this classification; do not confuse gross sales with the required turnover measure. Transition benefits are a separate question.

self_check.prompt_text: If investment fits micro but turnover exceeds its ceiling, is micro established?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Both criteria must fit the same category.

items.title: Send each issue to the institution with the relevant function
items.core_explanation_md:
The National Board is a policy and development forum: it examines sector conditions, reviews programmes, recommends improvements and advises on the statutory funds. It is not the dispute-resolution Council. Its head office is Delhi and it must meet at least once every three months. A person associated to advise it can join the relevant discussion without a vote.

The Advisory Committee supports the classification and advisory work under section 7, chaired by the Ministry Secretary with the specified official and association representation. Sections 9-14 separately enable development measures, RBI-guided credit policy, procurement preferences and funding. None of these makes every MSME application an automatic loan sanction.

self_check.prompt_text: Does the National Board decide an unpaid supplier invoice through arbitration?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. That dispute route belongs to the Facilitation Council framework.

items.title: Read the filing framework with its notification
items.core_explanation_md:
The original section 8 describes discretionary memorandum filing for micro/small enterprises and medium service enterprises, and mandatory filing for the specified medium manufacturing enterprises. It delegates the form and procedure to notification. This statutory history should not be presented as instructions to use an obsolete form today.

The later Udyam framework in the retained 2020 notification provides online registration, no filing fee and a single registration that may contain multiple manufacturing or service activities. Its original historical EM/UAM transition dates are not taught here as current deadlines. Identity, tax-data and later amendment details must be checked for the date and entity involved.

self_check.prompt_text: Should a book extract on the original memorandum be used as a current portal filing guide?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Read the statute with the applicable later notifications and date.

items.title: Build the payment clock from the delivery record
items.core_explanation_md:
A delivery date, an objection date and an objection-removal date serve different purposes. Under section 2(b), a written acceptance objection made within fifteen days of delivery or service changes the relevant acceptance day to the day the supplier removes it. Without a written objection within that window, deemed acceptance uses the actual delivery or service date.

The appointed day is the day immediately after the fifteen-day period from acceptance or deemed acceptance. Preserve the correspondence: a buyer cannot simply invent a later internal approval date and use it as a substitute for the statutory facts. Actual disputes about dates and eligibility still require evidence.

self_check.prompt_text: Does an internal approval delay automatically reset deemed acceptance?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The statutory objection conditions and actual dates control.

items.title: Forty-five days is a ceiling, not a universal grace period
items.core_explanation_md:
For an eligible supplier transaction, section 15 requires payment by the written agreed date; without such agreement, payment must occur before the appointed day. Even a written agreement cannot set a period beyond forty-five days from acceptance or deemed acceptance. A shorter valid agreed period remains meaningful: the maximum does not automatically replace it.

For delay under section 16, identify the proper start: the appointed day for the default route, or immediately after the agreed payment date for the agreement route. First establish the applicable acceptance facts. Do not calculate interest from invoice entry, loan sanction or financial-year closing simply because those dates are easier to find.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a ten-day written term become forty-five days automatically?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Forty-five days is the outer permitted period, not a replacement for every shorter agreement.

items.title: The reference is bank rate; the mechanism is monthly compounding
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 16 links the delayed-payment rate to three times the RBI-notified bank rate and requires compound interest with monthly rests. Do not substitute a loan rate, repo rate or a simple-interest convention merely because it is familiar. A private lower-rate term does not displace this statutory rule.

For a training problem with a constant stipulated annual bank rate and complete monthly periods, multiply that annual rate by three, divide by twelve for the assumed monthly rate, compound the outstanding amount and subtract principal to obtain interest. Live claims need actual rate changes, dates and applicable conventions; this exercise does not certify partial-month computation.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Convert the annual rate to the stated monthly rate; then compound monthly.

items.title: A reference starts a process; it is not an instant award
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 18 allows a party to refer the specified amount-due dispute to the Facilitation Council. The Council conducts or refers conciliation. If that conciliation fails and is terminated without settlement, the statutory route proceeds to arbitration conducted by the Council or a referred institution or centre. Do not label a failed negotiation an award.

The supplier-location jurisdiction provision can reach a buyer anywhere in India. The Act states ninety days from making a reference for its decision; this is not evidence that an actual file was decided in time. The State establishes Councils; their statutory membership range is three to five and the designated industry official chairs them. Later procedural amendments and case law remain review issues.

self_check.prompt_text: Does an out-of-state buyer alone defeat the supplier-location jurisdiction provision?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The provision expressly addresses a buyer located anywhere in India.

items.title: A challenge deposit is not a new discount on liability
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 19 addresses entertaining the stated application to set aside a decree, award or order when the appellant is not a supplier. The required deposit is seventy-five per cent of the amount in terms of that decree, award or order, in the manner directed by the court. It is not a general twenty-five per cent waiver or a promise of success on challenge.

Pending disposal, the court directs payment to the supplier of such percentage of the deposit as it considers reasonable, subject to conditions. Do not automatically treat the whole deposit as an unconditional final distribution. Keep the award amount, required deposit and any interim release separate.

self_check.prompt_text: Does depositing seventy-five per cent erase the remaining award amount?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The deposit is a procedural condition, not a discount or a merits decision.

items.title: Paying principal does not make the interest trail disappear
items.core_explanation_md:
For a buyer whose annual accounts must be audited under a law, section 22 requires the specified principal and interest disclosures, including separate year-end unpaid amounts and delayed-payment/further-interest information. A nil principal balance is not enough to conclude that no MSMED disclosure or unpaid interest remains.

Section 23 disallows deduction of interest payable or paid under the Act for income-tax computation. This card does not determine every tax consequence of the purchase principal. Section 24 gives sections 15-23 overriding effect over inconsistent laws. The penalty route also matters: section 27 distinguishes intentional section 8(1)/26(2) contraventions from an audited buyer breach of section 22, for which the stated fine is at least INR 10,000. Do not transpose the first-offence INR 1,000 ceiling to that separate buyer offence.

self_check.prompt_text: Does clearing principal necessarily clear statutory interest and all disclosure obligations?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Reconcile the interest and the statutory disclosure categories separately.

items.title: Choose the legal task before the remedy
items.core_explanation_md:
A stressed account can raise several different tasks. An acquisition of financial assets from an originator relates to securitisation; acquiring the relevant rights for realisation relates to asset reconstruction. Enforcing an existing security interest is a different task again. The Central Registry supports the recording framework; registration is not itself payment of the debt.

SARFAESI provides a statutory enforcement route with conditions, safeguards and exclusions. The possibility of acting without first obtaining a civil-court decree does not give an unrestricted right to seize anything owned by a debtor. Establish the creditor, debt, security, applicable asset and procedure before choosing the route.

self_check.prompt_text: Does an unpaid debt alone establish a power to seize any debtor property under SARFAESI?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The secured relationship, asset and statutory conditions must be established.

items.title: A statutory safeguard depends on the event that has happened
items.core_explanation_md:
A demand notice, consideration of objections and a possession measure are different events. In Hindon Forge the Supreme Court distinguishes the section 13(2) demand/section 13(3A) response stage from measures under section 13(4). Its conclusion recognises approach to the DRT under section 17 at the possession-notice stage described in rule 8(1) and 8(2).

Do not turn this into a requirement to wait for actual physical dispossession or completed sale before seeking that statutory remedy. Nor should it be read as saying every earlier letter is already a section 13(4) measure. This card describes the identified decision; later authority and the facts of a live proceeding require review.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The specified possession-notice stage can suffice.

items.title: Map the legal roles in the file
items.core_explanation_md:
In this Act, a familiar word can have a special meaning. The defined Board is SEBI, not the lending bank board. Borrower can include the described guarantor or person who provides mortgage or pledge security for financial assistance, as well as the person receiving the assistance. A person need not have received the cash personally to require analysis under the definition.

Bank and financial institution are statutory categories, including the applicable enumerated or notified bodies. Do not assume every finance business qualifies because its name contains finance. DRT and DRAT are also different: the Tribunal and appellate institution must not be collapsed into one forum. Detailed jurisdiction and remedy conditions belong to the relevant provisions.

self_check.prompt_text: Does no cash received personally settle that a guarantor is outside the defined borrower?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The definition extends beyond the immediate recipient of the assistance.

items.title: Credit facility, claim and collateral answer different questions
items.core_explanation_md:
Financial assistance describes the credit support: the definition reaches beyond a cash loan to the stated advances, subscriptions, guarantees, letters of credit and other facilities. The courseware also records the described asset-finance, intangible-right and debt-security additions. Financial asset concerns the debt, receivable or specified right, which can include an unsecured claim.

Property is wider than land: it can include movables, rights to payment, future receivables and the described intangible rights. A claim being a financial asset does not prove that it carries enforceable security over a particular property. Examine the security relationship separately; otherwise a definition about transferable claims becomes an unsupported enforcement conclusion.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Financial assets include the specified unsecured claims and other rights.

items.title: Draw the security relationship before taking action
items.core_explanation_md:
The security agreement is the arrangement creating the relevant interest; it can include the described mortgage by deposit of title deeds. The secured asset is the property carrying that interest. Secured debt is the debt protected by it. The secured creditor is the qualifying holder under the statutory definition, which extends to the specified ARC and trustee situations. These are related terms with different jobs.

The security-interest definition must be read with the section 31 exclusions. A party can hold a financial claim without having a statutory enforcement right over every borrower asset. Check what interest was actually created, for whose benefit, over what property and whether an exclusion applies.

self_check.prompt_text: Does an unsecured balance become secured merely because the creditor is a bank?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. A qualifying creditor does not replace the need for the actual security relationship.

items.title: Possession and the statutory exclusion matter
items.core_explanation_md:
Hypothecation describes the specified charge over existing or future movable property without delivering possession to the creditor. It includes the stated floating-charge and crystallisation situation. The fact that the borrower continues using the goods therefore does not by itself disprove the hypothecation.

Do not merge this with a pledge merely because both involve movables. The SARFAESI section 31(b) exclusion expressly concerns pledge of movables within section 172 of the Contract Act. A valid security may have a remedy under another legal framework while being excluded from this Act. Exclusion from SARFAESI is not a declaration that the underlying pledge is void.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a pledge exclusion mean that every valid pledge debt is cancelled?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Act applicability and the validity or other remedies of a pledge are different questions.

items.title: A status label is one input to a legal decision
items.core_explanation_md:
For the ordinary loan route described in this unit, nonpayment and the applicable non-performing classification matter. An internal overdue label is not a substitute for the asset-classification rules applicable to the lender and account. The courseware also records a distinct debt-security demand branch; do not apply one route mechanically to every instrument.

Even an established NPA does not create missing security, remove exclusions, satisfy notices or prove that every measure was lawful. Keep the definition-level status and the operative enforcement conditions in separate parts of the file. This is a legal-concept lesson, not a certification of a lender current prudential classification instructions.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Those are separate statutory and factual checks.

items.title: Follow the claim from transferor to acquirer
items.core_explanation_md:
The originator is the owner of the financial asset acquired for securitisation or reconstruction. The obligor is the person bearing the described payment or discharge obligation in relation to that asset, including the borrower. These roles describe opposite sides of the claim; an originator does not become the debtor merely by transferring it.

Asset reconstruction concerns acquisition of the specified rights for realisation. Acquisition can change who holds or administers rights, while the obligation itself still needs payment or another legally effective discharge. Notifications to obligors, discharge protection and the transfer procedure require the separate operative provisions; do not infer them from a definition alone.

self_check.prompt_text: Does transfer of the claim itself prove the obligor has paid it?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Transfer and discharge are different events.

items.title: Investor evidence is not the same as full ownership of each collateral item
items.core_explanation_md:
A scheme invites subscription to security receipts. The receipt evidences the described undivided right, title or interest in the financial asset involved in securitisation. It should not be described as automatic personal ownership of every underlying collateral item, a bank deposit, or a guarantee that the claim will be collected.

Qualified buyer is a defined category, read with applicable notifications rather than an assumption that every retail investor qualifies. Sponsor is a different role, based on holding not less than ten per cent of the ARC paid-up equity. A person holding a security receipt is not automatically a sponsor: an interest in the financial asset and an equity holding in the company are different interests.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Sponsor status uses the specified paid-up equity holding, not mere receipt ownership.

items.title: A registry entry and a Tribunal order do different work
items.core_explanation_md:
The Central Registry is part of the statutory transaction-recording framework. DRT is the Tribunal and DRAT the appellate institution identified by the Act. A filed record does not mean the Registrar has adjudicated every dispute about debt, title, validity or priority. Conversely, a Tribunal filing is not a substitute for every required security registration.

When preparing a legal checklist, assign each task to the right system: recording a security transaction, determining a challenge and pursuing an appeal are separate acts. Exact registry timing, priority, remedy periods and deposit rules must use the applicable amended provisions; the historical compilation retained here is not a current procedural checklist.

self_check.prompt_text: Can proof of a registry filing be treated as a final Tribunal determination of the debt?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Recording and adjudication serve different functions.

items.title: A company certificate is not the ARC regulatory permission
items.core_explanation_md:
Incorporation creates the company; it does not by itself authorise the statutory ARC business. Section 3 registration and the applicable RBI conditions require separate evidence. Professional, fit-and-proper and prudential checks are substantive requirements rather than a reason to assume that incorporation completed the process.

For the retained RBI Directions snapshot updated 10 March 2026, the minimum ongoing NOF is INR 300 crore, with the stated existing-ARC deadline of 31 March 2026. The courseware two-crore statutory wording must not be taught as this RBI floor. Resolution-applicant activity has a separate INR 1,000 crore NOF condition and further requirements. Meeting a capital number alone does not establish every permission.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Registration, applicable prudential requirements and activity-specific conditions remain separate.

items.title: Cancellation is a reasoned regulatory process
items.core_explanation_md:
The cancellation grounds described in section 4 include cessation of the business and the specified failures concerning investment, registration conditions, directions, accounts, inspection and prior approval. The opportunity to take corrective steps is qualified: its exceptions and the recorded public-interest reasons must be read in the applicable text. Do not simplify this into either a universal hearing guarantee or a claim that every default permits unexplained cancellation.

items.title: Payment routing needs the notice record
items.core_explanation_md:
Acquisition of the financial asset and notice to the obligor are different events. Section 6 describes the acquisition-notice route and the payment/discharge effect when the notified obligor pays the ARC. items.title: A menu of measures is not permission to skip their conditions

items.title: Check the route, then the notice and response
items.core_explanation_md:

items.title: Identify which power carries which restriction
items.core_explanation_md:
Section 13(4) separates possession of secured assets, the qualified takeover of business management, appointing a manager and directing the specified third-party payments. The substantial-business and severability provisos belong to the management-takeover clause 13(4)(b). Moving them into the ordinary possession clause changes the legal test.

Section 13 also distinguishes recovery of a balance after realisation and the separate guarantor/pledge routes. After the demand notice, the restriction on transferring the identified secured assets includes an ordinary-course-of-business exception and otherwise requires prior written creditor consent. Neither possession nor default should be presented as automatic creditor ownership of every borrower property. Detailed sale-rule compliance remains a separate step.

items.core_explanation_md:
A section 14 request is supported by the authorised officer affidavit addressing the specified claim, valid security, limitation, default, classification, notice, objection treatment and compliance facts.
